pages.text: Mei the timid baby goat pressed their nose to the lodge window. Outside, the four dug a snow cave. "I want to sit in there with them." Snow had piled up all night.
Mei opened the door and took one step. Sinking down, right to the tummy! The orange scarf ends drooped across the snow.
The four were bigger than Mei, so snow reached only their knees. Only Mei was stuck and couldn't move. "I'm too small."
Mei sat alone by the lodge stove. Laughter kept coming through the window. Mei held both scarf ends tightly.
Grandma Bear walked toward the snow cave, pressing big footprints into the snow. They led all the way from the lodge door. Then she turned and waited for Mei.
Mei stepped into each big footprint and reached the cave. But the four struggled at the entrance. Leo the know-it-all fox had his shoulders stuck.
"I'll try going in." Mei slipped through the narrow entrance. Outside, only orange scarf ends showed. From inside came Mei's voice. "Small can do things too!"
Inside, Mei pushed snow out of the cave. The narrow entrance grew wider, little by little. Leo tried putting his shoulders in again.
All five sat in a row inside. "One, little Mei slips in first! Two, big Leo shovels snow! Three, all sit together!" The five filled the cave.

Grandma sat at the entrance and gently touched her forehead to Mei's. "Being small doesn't mean you can't. There are things you can do because you're small." Mei waved their scarf. "Small can do things too!"
